title: Series Arc Fault Detection Using Differential Higher-Order Cumulants and Symmetric Stacked Autoencoder
relevance_reason: The paper is entirely about electrical arc fault detection in power systems; the phrase 'feature vector database' appears only in the trivial sense of storing extracted feature vectors for ML training, with no discussion of vector database technology, indexing structures, or similarity search.
research_focus: Detection of series arc faults in low-voltage distribution systems using differential sliding window higher-order cumulants (HoCs) combined with a symmetric stacked autoencoder (SAE) to reduce false alarm rates.
method: Differential sliding window higher-order cumulant feature extraction from current signals across seven typical loads, followed by classification using a symmetric stacked autoencoder trained via layer-wise pretraining with hyperparameter optimization.
application_domain: Electrical power systems, specifically series arc fault detection in low-voltage distribution circuits
results_summary: The paper proposes a HoC-SAE method for series arc fault diagnosis, extracting fourth-order cumulant features via a differential sliding window approach and classifying them with a three-hidden-layer stacked autoencoder (425 neurons total). Experimental results show a detection accuracy of 96.4% with a 0% false alarm rate across resistive, capacitive, switching, and inductive loads. The method outperforms wavelet-based and threshold-based approaches in suppressing non-arc-fault signals from appliances. The lightweight architecture is noted as amenable to fixed-point quantization and deployment on a 32-bit microcontroller, though recognition rates for dimmers and fluorescent lamps remain relatively low.
limitations: Fourth-order cumulant computation in the differential sliding window method requires fourth-power calculations, which are computationally intensive for embedded implementation; Recognition rates for dimmer and fluorescent lamp loads are relatively low due to their non-stationary current characteristics
research_gaps: Further research on simplifying the fourth-order cumulant computation for embedded deployment is required
